preamble:
Dear Freedom of Information Coordinator,

This is a request for records under the Municipal Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (MFIPPA). The $5.00 application fee is enclosed / has been paid.

I request electronic copies of records where they exist in electronic form. Please provide final versions of records; I am not requesting drafts. If any portion of a responsive record is withheld, please cite the specific exemption relied upon and disclose the remainder as required by s. 4(2). If estimated fees will exceed $25, please provide a fee estimate and advise me of fee-waiver provisions before proceeding, as required following the 2026 amendments — I am open to narrowing the scope of this request to reduce fees or processing time. Please note the amended definition of 'record' expressly includes data stored digitally; system configuration values responsive to this request are records in that sense.
closing:
Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to your response within the statutory period of 45 business days.

Sincerely,
[Name]
[Mailing address]
[Email] · [Phone]

items: Records sufficient to identify the number and locations (street address or intersection) of any fixed (non-vehicle-mounted) automated licence plate recognition (ALPR) cameras installed, piloted, or approved for installation by the Toronto Police Service, from January 1, 2023 to present.
The final Privacy Impact Assessment(s) for the ALPR program, including any updates prepared for the integration of ALPR into the in-car camera system completed in 2024–2025.

Records showing the currently configured retention periods in the ALPR system for (a) non-hit plate reads, (b) hit records, and (c) associated audit logs — for example, a system configuration export, administrative settings document, or governance procedure stating the configured values.

Any agreements, memoranda of understanding, or system configuration records governing the sharing of ALPR data with other police services or agencies, including whether any vendor cross-agency data-sharing features are enabled or disabled.
Final audit or compliance reports concerning access to or searches of ALPR data, from January 1, 2024 to present.
Records sufficient to identify which initiatives funded under the 'AI Operationalization' line of the 2026 operating/capital budget involve ALPR or licence-plate data.

Statistical or aggregate records showing, for the period January 1, 2023 to present: (a) the number of internal investigations, professional standards investigations, or privacy breach investigations involving alleged unauthorized access to, or misuse of, ALPR data, CPIC, or other police databases; (b) the number of substantiated findings; and (c) the disciplinary outcomes by category (e.g., training, forfeiture of hours, demotion, dismissal, criminal charge). To be clear, I am not requesting the names or identifying information of any individual — aggregate counts and severed summaries are responsive to this item. I also request any reports to the Police Services Board concerning misuse of ALPR or database access, and records showing whether and how often proactive audits of ALPR queries are conducted (audit policy, frequency, and the most recent audit report, severed as required).

requests.preamble:
Dear Freedom of Information Coordinator,

This is a request under MFIPPA. The $5 fee has been paid. Please provide final records in electronic form. If any portion is withheld, cite the specific exemption and sever the remainder (s. 4(2)). If fees will exceed $25, send an estimate first; I will narrow scope if needed. Digitally stored data, including system configuration values, are records for the purposes of this request.

requests.region: York Region (Vaughan, Markham, Richmond Hill, Newmarket, Aurora)
items: ALPR coverage. A record showing which of the CCTV sites published on the Community Safety Data Portal have ALPR enabled, and whether York Regional Police operates any ALPR-capable camera — fixed, trailer-mounted, temporary or otherwise — that is not published on that portal. If ALPR is enabled at all published sites and there are no unpublished ones, a written statement saying so is a complete answer.

Configured retention. Records showing the retention period currently configured in the ALPR system for (a) plate reads that do not match the hot list, (b) reads that do match, and (c) ALPR audit logs. A configuration export, an administrative settings page, or a governance document stating the values is sufficient. Also: the record identifying which position or role can change those values, and whether a change requires anything beyond a system administrator's action.

The hot list, and sharing. (a) The agreement, memorandum or terms of use under which York Regional Police receives and uses the provincial stolen vehicle hot list; (b) the current state of any setting permitting another agency to search York Regional Police ALPR data through the Axon platform, and the identity of any agency with such access.

The 6.19% analysis. The Business Intelligence Unit analysis underlying the June 25, 2025 board report's finding of 455 violent crimes within one kilometre of CCTV-equipped intersections (May 1, 2024 to May 1, 2025) against 485 the previous period: the methodology, the offence categories counted, the per-location figures, and the results of the evaluation of adjacent areas to CCTV locations referred to in that report.

Privacy Impact Assessment. The final Privacy Impact Assessment for the CCTV program and the final assessment, addendum or update prepared for the ALPR integration approved June 25, 2025 — or a written statement that no assessment was prepared for the ALPR integration.

Grant record. The Ontario CCTV Grant agreement or transfer-payment terms for the $255,000 contribution agreed in April 2025, including any reporting obligations to the Province, and Appendix A to the June 25, 2025 board report if the locations it names differ from those now published on the portal.

Aggregate audit and misuse statistics. For January 1, 2023 to present: aggregate counts of internal, professional standards or privacy investigations involving alleged unauthorized access to or misuse of police information systems, the number substantiated, and the disciplinary outcomes by category — no names or identifying information. Plus the current audit policy for ALPR and CCTV queries, and the most recent completed audit report, severed as required.

events.label: Acknowledged — file 26-1898, clarification requested
events.note: York Regional Police's Access & Privacy unit acknowledged the request and asked us to clarify or narrow all seven items before any search begins, warning that search time is billable under the Police Services Board bylaw and that a fee estimate will follow if the threshold is exceeded. Reply due within 30 days (Oct 9). Answering it turned up the records: the Board approved putting ALPR on every camera on June 25, 2025, YRP publishes all 58 active camera locations as open data, and the "6% crime reduction" is 30 fewer violent crimes — 455 against 485 — with no control area published. Narrowed reply drafted; six of seven items shrank, one was withdrawn outright.

events.label: Clarification answered — scope narrowed, one item withdrawn
events.note: Replied the same day, 7:16 p.m. Every one of their eight questions answered, six items narrowed, and the camera-locations item withdrawn entirely — York Regional Police already publishes all 58 active sites as open data, which we had been carrying on the map as anonymous crowd pins. Supplied the citations they asked for: their own June 25, 2025 board report for the $255K Ontario CCTV Grant and the ALPR approval, and the Markham Review of Nov 16, 2025 for the 6% claim, whose source figure is 455 violent crimes against 485. Noted that narrowing a request that already described the records does not restart the statutory clock, and asked what response date they are working to.

requests.preamble:
Narrowed on September 9, 2026, in reply to York Regional Police's clarification letter on file 26-1898. What follows is the live scope; it replaces the seven items sent on September 1, which are still published below.

The narrowing was possible because most of the original letter turned out to be answerable from public records. York Regional Police publishes every active camera location as open data; the Board's June 25, 2025 report carries the ALPR approval, the Axon partnership, the $255,000 Ontario CCTV Grant and the crime-reduction figure — 455 violent crimes within 1 km of a camera against 485 the year before. So the locations item was withdrawn outright, the Board-records item was withdrawn, and the rest was cut to the part nobody publishes: what the system is configured to do.

I request the following, and I am content for security-sensitive material to be severed:
requests.closing:

Sincerely,
[Name]
[Email]
